annotations.annotation_text: Page 115 opens Book 1, Chapter 5 ("The Letter from the Midden") during the Age of Gods phase. This passage continues Biddy Doran the Hen scratching up the mysterious letter from the dump, the Book of Kells as model for textual exegesis, featuring The Hen (Biddy Doran), ALP. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "letter" on page 115 ("The Letter from the Midden"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within Biddy Doran the Hen scratching up the mysterious letter from the dump, the Book of Kells as model for textual exegesis. During this Age of Gods phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Deane, Vincent, et al. The Finnegans Wake Notebooks at Buffalo. https://www.brepols.net

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 115 ("The Letter from the Midden"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Gods dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
